key_insight: Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ redox chemistry pins the Fermi level, overcoming self-limiting nitrogen incorporation in perovskite-type oxynitrides.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level engineering offers a strategy for controlling oxynitride composition during synthesis, although solar-cell performance is not evaluated here.
method: Combine theoretical modelling with experimental characterisation of titanium oxynitrides.
Tune A-site composition in Eu–Ba and Eu–Ca perovskite-derived oxynitrides.
Use defect energetics and charge compensation to explain nitrogen uptake.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nitrogen uptake up to 0.03 per formula unit in barium titanium oxynitrides versus up to 0.65 in Eu-containing compositions by hot gas extraction, with Fermi-level pinning approximately 2.9 eV above the valence-band maximum.
watch_item: Further nitrogen incorporation remains limited by bond-angle distortion within Ti(O,N)₆ octahedra.
paper_title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
